main_text.p: rectificetur & corrigatur accensoigne, sufficienti-giis ex ligno & baccis juniperi, thu e. mastiche.Igne con tra aeré infectā nihil efficacius;

Igne enim contra aerem infectum nihil efficacius; vapores enim absorbet & dissipat. Unde Hippocrates, magnam illam luem Athenis & totum fere Graciæ igne publicis in plateis & computis accenso propulsauit: idem saepe Thaletem Milefium facisse reperiō. Ignes debent construi ex lignis juniperi, abietis, ypreffi vetularum, tamarifci, quernis, fagi-nis & similibus. Ligna refiniferarum arborum omnibus aliis præstant.

Præstat etiam in ipso sanitatis statu præserim literis operam navantibus, singulis horis matutinus os & palatam diligenter aquà pura cum aceti modico vel pura rosacea abluere, vel aceto aquarofarum mixto, vel vino aquà rosarum temperato quod postremum oculis clarificandis optimum est. Frontis denique, temporum nariumque spersio aquâ rosar. vel lauendula, vel etiam aceto rosarum opitimum spiritum fomentum est: & tatum de aere nobis offuso, ac inuitis etiam ad corporis vigorem tutelamque, inspirando dixisse sufficiat.
main_text.head: CAP. III.
De cibo, & potu, secundum locum inter Sanitatis prorogandæ præcepta & capita obtinentibus.
main_text.p: Onstat quotidie aliquid de corporis nostri substantia decedere, viuereq; hominem

page.notes: The left-margin notes are reconstructed from their visible fragments ("Igne con / tra aeré / infectā / nihil ef- / ficacius.") and may be incomplete. The heading of the second block is partly obscured. Several words in the first column are uncertain, including the long-s forms and the abbreviation "&"; the transcription of the Greek-style initial and some tall letters is doubtful. The running head is taken from the page header "De Vita". Some lines near the bottom ("minem") are partly cut off by the page edge.
